text: The account holder Hamid Shah holds account PK**BAHL****5384 which was opened on 25 January 2020. The subject is a Medical sales officer (salaried) with a declared monthly income of PKR 220,000 per month. During the activity window from 1 May 2026 to 25 May 2026, there were 14 credits totalling PKR 18,216,000 and 4 debits totalling PKR 14,854,000. The account received 13 cash deposits totalling PKR 17,996,000 at four branches (Clifton Branch, DHA Phase 6 Branch, Gulshan-e-Iqbal Branch, Saddar Branch). Tazama raised an alert on 25 May 2026, scoring 320 against a threshold of 300. Nine of the 13 cash deposits (69%) were between PKR 1,600,000 and PKR 1,999,999, totalling PKR 16,337,000, which is just below the reporting threshold of PKR 2,000,000. The cash deposits were made across four different branches, indicating a spread of activity. There were more than one cash deposit on two days (11 May 2026, 25 May 2026). Credits in the activity window were 82.8 times the declared monthly income of PKR 220,000 per month. A branch employee noted that the customer asked why deposits of PKR 2 million or more need extra paperwork and declined to explain the source of the cash. These patterns are consistent with suspected structuring, given the repeated near‑threshold deposits, branch spread, multiple daily deposits, high cash volume relative to declared income, and the customer’s reluctance to explain the source of funds. PKR 7,434,000 was sent to Sheraz Traders (PK**SHER****1518, Synthetic Bank A) in 2 transactions. PKR 7,420,000 was sent to Crescent Imports (PK**CRES****1592, Synthetic Bank A) in 2 transactions. Debits equal to 82% of credits were paid out with a median of 15.3 hours between the latest credit and each debit. Screening on 28 May 2026 found no match on sanctions, PEP or adverse‑media lists. The account was placed under enhanced monitoring pending the reporting decision, with no contact made with the customer about this review.
